question: Who has the distinction of serving as the Chief Justice of India, President and the Vice president? (RRB NTPC Tier I (11/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: Justice M Hidayatullah
Justice Bhagwati
Justice H.J.Kania
Justice Mehr Chand Mahajan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Justice M Hidayatullah

Explanation:
Justice Mohammad Hidayatullah is the only person in India to have served as Chief Justice of India, Vice President, and President. He served as the Chief Justice from 1968 to 1970. In 1977, he became the Vice President, and in 1979, he became the acting President of India. This unique distinction remains unmatched in Indian constitutional history. His tenure as acting President was brief, but his contributions to Indian judiciary and governance are significant. This fact is crucial for understanding the highest offices in India.

question: Which among the following is NOT a qualification to become a Vice President of India? (RRB NTPC Tier I (16/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: Citizen of India
Above 35 years of age
Possess the Membership of LokSabha
He or she must be qualified for election as a Member of the Rajya Sabha or the Council of States.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Possess the Membership of LokSabha

Explanation:
The office of the Vice President of India is provided under Articles 63-67 of the Indian Constitution. The qualifications to become Vice President are mentioned in Article 66. According to this, the person must be a citizen of India, must have completed the age of 35 years, and must be qualified to be elected as a member of the Rajya Sabha. Membership of the Lok Sabha is not a qualification because the Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Thus, possessing Lok Sabha membership is not a requirement.

☛ Election of Vice President → by single transferable vote
☛ Removal of Vice President → by resolution of Rajya Sabha
☛ Salary of Vice President → determined by Parliament
☛ Function of Vice President → as Chairman of Rajya Sabha
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति बनने की योग्यता नहीं है? (RRB NTPC Tier I (16/04/2016) Shift 3)

Solution: सही उत्तर है लोकसभा की सदस्यता

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 63-67 में उपराष्ट्रपति के पद का प्रावधान है। उपराष्ट्रपति बनने की योग्यताएं अनुच्छेद 66 में दी गई हैं। इनके अनुसार, व्यक्ति को भारत का नागरिक होना चाहिए, उसकी आयु 35 वर्ष से अधिक होनी चाहिए, और वह राज्य सभा का सदस्य चुने जाने योग्य होना चाहिए। लोकसभा की सदस्यता उपराष्ट्रपति बनने के लिए आवश्यक नहीं है, क्योंकि उपराष्ट्रपति राज्य सभा के पदेन सभापति होते हैं। इस प्रकार, लोकसभा की सदस्यता योग्यता नहीं है।

question: Which is not true for the Government of India Act 1919?A. The Act had a separate preamble.B. This Act has made the Central Legislature liable.C. The Act has provided the Public Service Commission in India.D. The Act covered 20 years from 1919 to 1939. (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: B
C
D
A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is D

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, had a separate preamble stating the British government's aim to establish responsible government in India. This Act did not make the Central Legislature responsible; rather, it introduced dyarchy in provincial governments. It provided for the establishment of a Public Service Commission, which was later set up in 1926. The Act did not cover 20 years from 1919 to 1939; it was replaced by the Government of India Act 1935. Thus, option D is incorrect.

☛ What system of government did this Act introduce? → Dyarchy
☛ Into how many parts were provincial subjects divided under this Act? → Two (Reserved and Transferred)
☛ Which Commission was provided for under this Act? → Public Service Commission
☛ Which Act was replaced by the Government of India Act 1919? → Government of India Act 1909
question_hi: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के लिए कौन सा सही नहीं है?A. अधिनियम की एक अलग प्रस्तावना थी।B. इस अधिनियम ने केंद्रीय विधानमंडल को उत्तरदायी बनाया है।C. अधिनियम ने भारत में लोक सेवा आयोग प्रदान किया है।D. अधिनियम ने 1919 से 1939 तक 20 वर्ष को कवर किया। (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 3)
options_hi: B
C
D
A
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है D

Explanation:
भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919, जिसे मोंटेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार भी कहा जाता है, में एक अलग प्रस्तावना थी जिसमें ब्रिटिश सरकार का उद्देश्य भारत में उत्तरदायी सरकार स्थापित करना बताया गया। इस अधिनियम ने केंद्रीय विधानमंडल को उत्तरदायी नहीं बनाया, बल्कि प्रांतीय सरकारों में द्वैध शासन लागू किया। इसी अधिनियम के तहत लोक सेवा आयोग की स्थापना का प्रावधान किया गया, जिसे बाद में 1926 में स्थापित किया गया। यह अधिनियम 1919 से 1939 तक 20 वर्षों के लिए नहीं था; बल्कि इसे 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किया गया। विकल्प D गलत है क्योंकि अधिनियम 1939 तक प्रभावी नहीं रहा।

question: On which date is the Constitution Day of India celebrated? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/12/2020) Shift 1)
options: 26th January
26th November
15th August
14th April
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26th November

Explanation:
In India, Constitution Day is celebrated annually on 26th November. On this day in 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Indian Constitution. It is also known as National Law Day. The Constitution came into effect on 26th January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day. Constitution Day has been observed at the government level since 2015. The purpose of this day is to spread awareness about the values and ideals of the Constitution.

☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed? → 1946
☛ Since when has Constitution Day been celebrated? → 2015

question: Which part of the Constitution of India contains Fundamental Rights of the citizens of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (30/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: Part 2
Part 4
Part 3
Part 1
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part 3

Explanation:
Part 3 of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) contains the Fundamental Rights of citizens. These rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the Supreme Court or High Courts for their enforcement. The Fundamental Rights include Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32). These rights are inspired by the United States Constitution. Fundamental Rights are not absolute and can be restricted for reasons of national security, public order, etc.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the title of Part 3? → Fundamental Rights
☛ Which country's constitution inspired Fundamental Rights? → USA
☛ Which Article deals with Right to Constitutional Remedies? → Article 32
☛ To whom are Fundamental Rights applicable? → All citizens (some to foreigners too)
☛ Which Article is NOT related to Right to Equality? → Article 19
question_hi: भारत के संविधान के किस भाग में भारत के नागरिकों के मौलिक अधिकार शामिल हैं? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (30/12/2020) Shift 2)
options_hi: भाग 2
भाग 4
भाग 3
भाग 1
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग 3

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग 3 में अनुच्छेद 12 से 35 तक मौलिक अधिकार शामिल हैं। ये अधिकार न्यायसंगत हैं, अर्थात नागरिक इनके उल्लंघन पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय या उच्च न्यायालय जा सकते हैं। मौलिक अधिकारों में समानता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14-18), स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 19-22), शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 23-24), धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 25-28), सांस्कृतिक और शैक्षिक अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 29-30), और संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 32) शामिल हैं। भारत में मौलिक अधिकार अमेरिकी संविधान से प्रेरित हैं।

question: The first high court of India was established in _______. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Kolkata
Delhi
Mumbai
Punjab
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kolkata

Explanation:
The first high court of India was the Calcutta High Court, established on July 1, 1862, under the Indian High Courts Act 1861. It was followed by the Bombay and Madras High Courts later in the same year. The Calcutta High Court was originally located at Fort William and later renamed as the Kolkata High Court. It is one of the oldest high courts in India and its jurisdiction covers West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

☛ When was the Calcutta High Court established? → July 1, 1862
☛ Under which act were high courts established in India? → Indian High Courts Act 1861
☛ What was the original name of the Calcutta High Court? → Fort William High Court
☛ Which other high courts were established in 1862? → Bombay and Madras High Courts

दिल्ली

Explanation:

question: Name the minister who resigned during the India China war in 1962? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/01/2021) Shift 2)

Lal Bahadur Shastri
V. K. Krishna Menon
Sardar Patel

Explanation:
During the India-China war of 1962, the then Defence Minister V. K. Krishna Menon resigned taking responsibility for India's defeat. He was serving in Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet. The Indian Army suffered a major setback in the war, leading to widespread public and parliamentary outrage. Under this pressure, Krishna Menon stepped down from his post. This was a significant event in Indian politics, paving the way for subsequent reforms in defence strategy and policy.

question: Government of India Act, 1935 introduced: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Provincial autonomy
Self-autonomy
Union territories
Dyrachy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provincial autonomy

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1935 was a significant act passed by the British Parliament. It introduced provincial autonomy, granting provincial governments extensive powers over internal affairs in their regions. The act ended dyarchy in provinces and gave more authority to provincial legislatures. It also envisaged a federal structure, though the federal part never came into effect. This act provided autonomy to provincial governments, leading to provincial elections in 1937, in which the Congress and other parties formed governments. The act marked a major step in India's constitutional development.

question: How many ministers can be included in the council of Ministers of the Union? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Ten to fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of People
Fifty percent of the total number of members of the House of People
As many as wished by the Prime Minister of India
Fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of People
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of People

Explanation:
According to Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha (House of the People). This ceiling was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. The purpose is to limit the size of the Council of Ministers and enhance administrative efficiency. Based on the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha (550), the maximum number of ministers can be 82. This provision ensures a balanced and effective executive.

question: Which is the most important feature of federal government adopted by India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: The state government has more power than the union government.
The jurisdiction of all governments is the same.
The relationship between the state and the center should be based on cooperation.
The center is financially dependent on states.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The relationship between the state and the center should be based on cooperation

Explanation:
The most important feature of federal government adopted by India is cooperative federalism, where the center and states work together. The Indian Constitution, inspired by the Canadian model, divides powers with a strong center. However, in practice, a cooperative relationship between center and states is crucial. India's federal structure is indestructible, and states cannot secede. This cooperative approach ensures national unity and effective governance. Other options are incorrect because states do not have more powers than the union, jurisdictions are not identical, and the center is not financially dependent on states. The essence of Indian federalism lies in cooperation, not confrontation.

question: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Bill, 2019 was introduced in Rajya Sabha by the Minister of Home Affairs, Mr. Amit Shah. When did this act of Parliament receive the assent of the President? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (15/02/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The words Socialist, Secular and Democratic Republic were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution through the 42nd Amendment in 1976. This amendment is often called the Mini Constitution. question: What does Article 243C deal with? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 1)

Protection of life and personal liberty

Explanation:
Article 243C is part of Part IX of the Indian Constitution, which deals with Panchayats. This article specifically addresses the composition of Panchayats, including the formation of Panchayats at the village, intermediate, and district levels. question: 'Right to Property' was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by which amendment to the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 48th
42th
44th
46th
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Amendment

Explanation:
The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India, passed in 1978, removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights (Article 19(1)(f) and 31) and made it a legal right under Article 300A. This amendment was enacted by the Morarji Desai government and came into effect on 20 June 1979. It stated that no person shall be deprived of his property except by authority of law. This change reduced the scope of judicial review in property matters and transformed the right from a fundamental right to a constitutional right, thereby allowing the government to acquire property for public purposes more easily.

question: A revised version of the 'India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement' was adopted by the two countries under which amendment to the Construction of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (15/02/2021) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:
The revised version of the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) was adopted under the 100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015. This amendment modified the First Schedule of the Indian Constitution, enabling adjustment of borders in northeastern states like Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura. It facilitated the exchange of enclaves (adversely possessed territories) and resolved long-standing border disputes. Approximately 162 enclaves were exchanged, granting citizenship to displaced residents. The amendment was passed during the tenure of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and marked a historic milestone in India-Bangladesh relations.

question: Article 43 B in Part Ⅳ of the Constitution of India deals with: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Village panchayats
Cooperative societies
Rural business hubs
Forest development
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cooperative societies

Explanation:
Article 43B in Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) of the Constitution of India deals with cooperative societies. This article was added by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002. It directs the State to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies. The 97th Amendment gave constitutional status to cooperative societies and introduced Article 43B in Part IV, a new fundamental duty under Article 51A(k) in Part IVA, and a new chapter on cooperative societies in Part IXB.

question: The Ministry of Home Affairs of India is responsible for: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/03/2021) Shift 2)

question: As of December 2020, how many fundamental duties are enumerated in the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 9
11
7
8
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 11

Explanation:
Fundamental duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. Originally, there were 10 duties. Later, the 86th Amendment in 2002 added one more duty, making the total 11. These duties are enshrined in Part IV-A (Article 51A). As of December 2020, there are 11 fundamental duties, which include respecting the national flag and anthem, protecting the unity and integrity of India, safeguarding public property, and protecting the environment. Fundamental duties are not legally enforceable but serve as moral obligations for citizens.

question: Which of the following is related to the 61st Amendment of the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Advancement of economically weaker sections of citizens
Extended the period of reservation of seats
Incorporation of Goa, Daman and Diu as a union territory
Lowered the voting age of elections
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lowered the voting age of elections

Explanation:
The 61st Amendment (1988) to the Indian Constitution reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years for elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. It amended Article 326, which defines adult suffrage. This amendment aimed to empower youth and increase political participation. Other options: Advancement of economically weaker sections relates to the 103rd Amendment; extension of reservation period is linked to 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th Amendments; and incorporation of Goa, Daman and Diu as a union territory is associated with the 12th Amendment (1962).

question: Provincial autonomy was prescribed under  Government of India Act of: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1935
1920
1947
1937
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1935

Explanation:
Provincial autonomy was prescribed under the Government of India Act of 1935. This Act granted provincial governments control over their subjects, though provincial governors retained special powers. It was a major reform in Indian administration, allowing provinces to move towards self-governance. The Act established provincial legislatures and a council of ministers responsible to the public. However, the central government still held most powers. The Act came fully into force in 1937. It marked a significant step in the constitutional development of India.

question_hi: भारतीय शासन अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता किस वर्ष निर्धारित की गई थी? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 2)

question_hi: भारत के किस राष्ट्रपति को मिसाइल मैन के रूप में जाना जाता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: ज़ाकिर हुसैन

डॉ. एपीजे अब्दुल कलाम

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है डॉ. एपीजे अब्दुल कलाम

Explanation:
डॉ. एपीजे अब्दुल कलाम को उनके मिसाइल प्रौद्योगिकी में योगदान के कारण 'मिसाइल मैन' कहा जाता है। वे भारत के 11वें राष्ट्रपति (2002-2007) थे और एक प्रसिद्ध वैज्ञानिक भी थे। उन्होंने SLV-III, Agni और Prithvi मिसाइलों के विकास में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। इसके अलावा, वे Pokhran-II परमाणु परीक्षणों में भी शामिल थे। उन्हें 1997 में भारत रत्न से सम्मानित किया गया। डॉ. कलाम का जन्म 15 अक्टूबर 1931 को धनुषकोडी, तमिलनाडु में हुआ था और उन्हें 'जनता के राष्ट्रपति' के रूप में भी जाना जाता है।
